h: Penguins, Otters and a Day in Brum
p: Some of the most popular residents here aren't fish at all. The centre is home to a colony of gentoo penguins, a lively bunch that zip through the water and waddle about on land, and it also cares for otters, which never fail to draw a crowd with their playful antics. Turtles, sharks and rays complete the line-up of big favourites. Feeding times and talks are the best chance to see the animals at their busiest, so check what's on when you arrive and plan your route around them.

Booking in advance is generally a good idea, especially in the school holidays and at weekends, and arriving earlier in the day can help you dodge the busiest spell. The visit is mostly flat and under cover, so it's an easy one for buggies and for anyone who struggles with long walks or bad weather.

Once you're done, Birmingham has bags of family-friendly options. The Library of Birmingham on Centenary Square is a striking modern building with garden terraces giving views over the city, and it's a great free stop. Thinktank, the science museum at Millennium Point, is packed with hands-on exhibits and a planetarium. A short trip out of the centre, Cadbury World in Bournville tells the story of chocolate with plenty of tasty treats along the way, while the Jewellery Quarter, a historic district of workshops and shops, is a fascinating place to explore on foot. Food lovers should seek out a balti, the dish Birmingham is famous for, to round off a cracking day in the city.
